title: Peer review and response
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of peer review and response
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: A concern about evidence, method or presentation
A mapping from comment to change or justified disagreement
Reducing a statement to the evidence actually available

blocks.text: Reviewer asks for a fitted-line baseline; author responds that the neural network is advanced, without a comparison.
The response lacks evidence. Add a fair comparison under the plan or narrow the claim to the existing baseline; record any new analysis as such.

Compare the intermediate evidence with the final statement. Explain why each number or decision follows from the stated inputs. The conclusion belongs to this scenario and procedure; changing the inputs, evaluation population or authority can change what it establishes. Retain the raw record so a later revision can be compared honestly.

guided_practice.title: Trace the worked case
guided_practice.prompt: Reviewer asks for a fitted-line baseline; author responds that the neural network is advanced, without a comparison. Show the intermediate steps and give the conclusion with its scope.
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: The response lacks evidence. Add a fair comparison under the plan or narrow the claim to the existing baseline; record any new analysis as such.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Reviewer notes missing failure counts; author deletes the limitation paragraph. What is an adequate response?
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Supply counts and denominators with raw evidence, retain the limitation and revise the claim. Deleting criticism does not resolve the evidence gap.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Agreement with a reviewer is not required, but a disagreement needs explicit reasoning and evidence.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: For each comment record concern, response, change location and new evidence if needed. If no new evidence exists, narrow the claim instead of promising an unperformed test.
